subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should `message.send` ignore schema-populated poll creation fields, or should the message tool schema be action/channel-scoped so ordinary sends never expose poll creation fields?
rationale: Current main intentionally rejects `pollQuestion` or `pollOption` on `send`, while the issue asks for ordinary sends not to be blocked by fields exposed through the shared schema; choosing strip/sanitize versus schema split changes the shared tool contract for all channels.

options.title: Action-scope the schema
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only when the `poll` action is available or selected, keeping ordinary sends small and preserving strict rejection for real misuse.

options.title: Sanitize send params
options.body: Strip poll creation params from `action="send"` before the guard, matching the open PR direction but making explicit poll-looking content on send silently ignored.

options.title: Keep current guard
options.body: Treat `pollQuestion` and `pollOption` on `send` as real poll intent and close only if maintainers decide the metadata-only fix is sufficient.

recommendation.title: Action-scope the schema
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only when the `poll` action is available or selected, keeping ordinary sends small and preserving strict rejection for real misuse.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main blame and PR history put this maintainer-routing decision closest to the current shared poll guard implementation.
